objections.title: Pre-spec file (Spec file: docs/dev/specs/spec-20260524-125921.md) contradicts ticket M1 on sourceSlotId — dev reads pre-spec FIRST
objections.description: The /dev workflow passes docs/dev/specs/spec-20260524-125921.md as the 'Spec file:' parameter. Dev reads the global spec before the BA ticket. The pre-spec Technical Hints (lines 174-182) explicitly instruct: add 'sourceSlotId: slotId' to ALL candidate card onDragStart payloads, and the proposed onDrop condition (line 189) gates on 'payload.sourceSlotId': '(payload.direction === "board" || payload.direction === "candidates") && payload.sourceSlotId && saveMutations'. If dev follows this instruction, candidate drops will include sourceSlotId, and the gated condition will work — but the source slot will be CLEARED because the board handlers contain 'saveMutations(dayNum, [{type:select, slot:payload.sourceSlotId, option_id:null}])' in the board branch. This is the exact state-corruption bug the ticket's M1 is trying to prevent. Ticket M1 says 'Do NOT add sourceSlotId to candidate payloads' but this appears AFTER the pre-spec which says the opposite. A developer reading both documents in /dev workflow order will encounter the dangerous instruction first.

conflict.pre_spec_says: Add sourceSlotId: slotId to candidate payloads; gate onDrop on payload.sourceSlotId
conflict.ticket_m1_says: Do NOT add sourceSlotId to candidate payloads

objections.required_fix: Either (a) remove the sourceSlotId instruction from the pre-spec Technical Hints before passing it to dev, or (b) add a prominent 'SUPERSEDED' banner to the pre-spec Technical Hints section citing the ticket M1 as the authoritative instruction, or (c) remove the pre-spec from the /dev Spec file: parameter entirely and rely solely on the ticket. The conflict must be resolved before dev receives any artifacts.

objections.title: AC1 must_not_contain 'option_id: null' check is too broad — rejects correct implementations
objections.description: AC1 check specifies must_not_contain: 'option_id: null' applied to the onDrop handler block. However, the correct board-to-board drag branch (which must be preserved and will remain in the same onDrop function) legitimately contains 'option_id: null' to clear the source slot when a board card is moved. If dev correctly implements a candidates branch while preserving the board branch, the AC1 check will FAIL even though the implementation is correct. The check needs to be scoped exclusively to the payload.direction === 'candidates' code branch, not the entire onDrop handler. Additionally, the AC1 given/when description says the drop target is '.slot-drop[data-slot-id="S"]' where S comes from the candidate's slotId. For meals candidates, slotId is 'meals-any' (a virtual ID), but board drop targets use real slot IDs ('breakfast', 'lunch', 'dinner'). The AC conflates candidate payload slotId with drop target data-slot-id.
objections.required_fix: Change AC1 check from must_not_contain: 'option_id: null' to must_not_contain_in_candidates_branch: 'option_id: null' with explicit scope: 'within the payload.direction === candidates conditional block only'. Also clarify the meals case: candidate payload carries slotId='meals-any' but the drop target data-slot-id is the actual meal slot; saveMutations should use the board slot's data-slot-id as slot, not the candidate's slotId.

objections.title: Symbol location errors in context JSON pre_existing_guards and imports_from
objections.description: The context JSON pre_existing_guards cites _isCompatible at line 497 (actual: line 2229) and MEAL_SLOTS at line 496 (actual: line 2228). The imports_from arrays reference _flashSuccess at line 504 (actual: line 2236) and _flashReject at line 518 (actual: line 2250). These are the 'do not touch' guards. Wrong line numbers mean dev cannot navigate to these guards by line number. While the function names are correct and dev can grep for them, the systematic off-by-~1730-lines error suggests the BA line-number extraction process has a fundamental bug (possibly reading a different version of the file, or the component definition offsets were miscounted from a partial file view).
objections.required_fix: Correct all line references in pre_existing_guards and imports_from in context JSON to match actual source. Investigate whether the same offset error affects any other line references in the context JSON beyond those already identified.

objections.title: No AC covers preservation of window.setEditorSelection bridge side effects
objections.description: The board onDrop handlers at lines 913, 998, 1084, 1170, 1320, and 1928 all call window.setEditorSelection (via the bridge) after saveMutations. This bridge handles cross-meal option copying into the target slot and accommodation preservation. The ticket's development approach for Bug A adds a candidates branch that calls saveMutations directly. No AC verifies that the bridge side effects are either (a) preserved in the candidates branch or (b) deliberately not needed for candidate-to-board drops. If dev adds saveMutations without the bridge call for candidates, meal option copies and accommodation merges may silently fail. This is a regression risk not covered by any acceptance criterion.

objections.required_fix: Add an AC or explicit note in M1/M2/M3 clarifying whether window.setEditorSelection bridge must be called in the candidates branch, and if so, with what parameters. If bridge is not needed for candidates, document the rationale explicitly so dev does not add it by mistake or skip it by oversight.

objections.title: AC1 slotId/toSlotId conflation for meals case
objections.description: AC1 given says 'candidate card with slotId=S' and when says 'drops onto .slot-drop[data-slot-id="S"]'. For activity and accommodation candidates, slotId in the payload matches the board drop target. But meals candidates use slotId='meals-any' (a virtual ID that is not a real board slot). The board meal slots are 'breakfast', 'lunch', 'dinner'. The drop overlay .slot-drop for a meal board slot will have data-slot-id='breakfast' (not 'meals-any'). The saveMutations call for meals must use the board slot's data-slot-id as the slot parameter, not the candidate's slotId. AC1 as written gives the incorrect impression that the candidate's own slotId is the drop target identifier.
objections.required_fix: Rewrite AC1 to distinguish: for activity/accommodation, toSlotId === candidate.slotId; for meals, toSlotId is the board drop target's data-slot-id (breakfast/lunch/dinner), not candidate.slotId ('meals-any'). saveMutations must use toSlotId (the board slot) not candidate.slotId for the slot parameter.

observations.title: AC5 grep_pattern catches only one bilingual literal out of multiple
observations.description: AC5 check uses grep_pattern: '早餐 / Breakfast' which catches only the breakfast label. The source file also contains '住宿 / Accommodation' (line 2415) and '餐饮 / Meals' (line 2461) as bilingual section headers inside #candidates-groups. A comprehensive grep should also target these strings. A post-fix grep of '/ [A-Z]' or '住宿 /' or '餐饮 /' would catch all bilingual patterns more reliably.
observations.recommendation: Expand AC5 grep_pattern to use a regex that catches all bilingual slash-strings, e.g., '[\u4e00-\u9fff]+ / [A-Za-z]+' or list each known bilingual string explicitly.

observations.title: AC6 has no executable grep check — only boolean assertion
observations.description: AC6 check is 'chrome_labels_english_only: true' with no executable grep_pattern. Unlike AC5 which has a concrete grep pattern (albeit narrow), AC6 has no mechanical verification recipe. Dev cannot confirm compliance without browser testing or a manual source scan.
observations.recommendation: Add an executable check to AC6, e.g., grep_pattern with a CJK unicode range '[\u4e00-\u9fff]' that must have zero matches in chrome label source strings (excluding data field values). This mirrors AC5's approach for the lang===base case.

observations.title: Loading/empty text i18n (M7) not explicitly called out in AC5/AC6 'then' clause
observations.description: AC5 and AC6 describe that panel title, section headers, and slot labels must be lang-aware. The loading text 'Loading candidates...' (line 2287) and empty text 'No candidates for this day.' (line 2309) are hardcoded English strings in CandidatesSidebar chrome. These are covered by M7 in the ticket but are not mentioned in the AC5/AC6 'then' clauses. Dev could pass the ACs while leaving loading/empty texts in English-only.
observations.recommendation: Add loading/empty text to AC5 and AC6 'then' clauses: 'loading text and empty state text must also respect lang parameter (no hardcoded English-only strings)'.

codex_consult.feedback_summary: Codex returned 10 findings. Key ones: (1) Pre-spec sourceSlotId conflict is BLOCKING, not merely potential confusion — dev reads Spec file first so this is a guaranteed implementation error path. (2) AC1 must_not_contain: 'option_id: null' is invalid when applied to full onDrop block — board-to-board branch legitimately contains it. (3) AC1 slotId/toSlotId conflation — meals candidate slotId 'meals-any' ≠ board drop target slot IDs. (4) Missing bridge side effects AC (window.setEditorSelection). (5) AC3 overlay vs overlay-plus-actual-drop not distinguished. (6) AC5/AC6 grep weakness for multiple bilingual strings. (7) Wrong 'non-UI' setup classification — CandidatesSidebar is a UI component. (8) Mobile dimensions not in AC3. (9) Missing test for .slot-drop overlay position/size relative to card. (10) AC2 three-card-type verification needs explicit test data.
